title: Dragonwilds Sync Helpy
subtitle: A living, system-by-system field guide shared by the website and desktop application.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.summary: First launch, Player Setup, profiles, and the recommended first run.
pages.intro: Dragonwilds Sync organizes local saves, connected Worlds, hosted servers, characters, mods, and Sync metadata around profiles.

sections.title: First launch
steps: Complete Player Setup and select the Dragonwilds installation.
Let Sync validate the game layout before installing or repairing shared prerequisites.
Pick a character after discovery completes.
Use Dragonwilds for Singleplayer, Co-Op, Dedicated hosting, profiles, and connections.

sections.title: Recommended first run
steps: Validate the local game folder in Dragonwilds > Game Setup.
Confirm Character saves and World associations under Profile.
Review the active profile and master repository under Mods.
Launch once, then open Sync only when ready to link or publish a verified World.

sections.title: Offline behavior
sections.body: The public Helpy page is cached by the browser. The desktop application also retains a packaged fallback when GitHub Pages is unavailable.

sections.title: Before first launch
sections.body: Launch Dragonwilds normally once so the game creates its expected folders. Back up irreplaceable saves before adopting a new manager, and verify the detected installation path before accepting repairs or migrations.

sections.title: When something fails
sections.body: Read the visible operation result first. Do not repeatedly click Launch, Save, or Sync while an operation is still active. Record the failed stage, active profile, and exact message before retrying.

tips: Visible operation errors remain authoritative.
Profiles isolate saves, mods, and runtime choices.
Refresh Helpy after a published documentation update.

sections.title: Helpy and Settings
sections.body: Helpy is this shared website page. Settings owns appearance, policy, integrations, updates, and system behavior.

sections.title: Persistent context
sections.body: The current profile, World, and character stay selected as Appys change. Confirm the visible context before Save, Pull Master, Remove, Stop Server, or any action that writes or replaces data.

sections.title: Search and operation feedback
sections.body: Each search filters its local workspace and keeps the magnifying glass inside the field. Toasts summarize operations, while status rows, progress details, and logs remain the authoritative diagnostic source.

tips: The navigation rail stays mounted between Appys.
A success message never replaces runtime verification.
Website and desktop Help use this same JSON.

pages.title: Worlds, Sync & Direct Connect
pages.summary: Private, connected, declared, and hosted World profiles.
pages.image_alt: Placard and horizontal World management views
pages.intro: A World profile keeps the correct save, mods, configuration, connection identity, artwork, and character association together.

sections.title: World views
steps: Placard and Horizontal are two views of the same profile.
Declared means a live fingerprint-verified heartbeat reached this WebHost.
Sync Ready means the endpoint supports Sync, not necessarily that it declared itself.

sections.title: Connecting
sections.body: Sync verifies identity, compares client-required files, applies the minimum safe update, verifies the final manifest, and only then launches Dragonwilds.

sections.title: Reviews
sections.body: Rating stars open the review window even when no reviews exist. Empty and unavailable states remain dismissible.

sections.title: Heartbeat projection
sections.body: Stale declarations expire automatically when they leave the host TTL or fingerprint evidence no longer passes.

sections.title: World identity
sections.body: Display names are presentation. Stable IDs and verified fingerprints prevent similarly named Worlds from becoming the same destination. A changed or unclaimed fingerprint is a new trust decision.

sections.title: Sync sequence
steps: Resolve the selected World and endpoint.
Verify the presented endpoint identity.
Retrieve public-safe requirements and compare manifests.
Transfer only approved differences into the active profile.
Verify the final manifest before launch.

sections.title: Direct Connect
sections.body: Direct Connect uses an explicit private endpoint without requiring a public listing. It does not bypass fingerprints, passwords, profile boundaries, or server-side permissions.

tips: Public metadata never includes passwords.
Duplicate launch clicks are rejected.
Timeouts return control to the launcher.

pages.title: Characters & RSDW Toolkit
pages.summary: Character selection, editors, Avatar preview, and safe writeback.
pages.intro: Profile > Characters uses the selected save as the hydration source for integrated RSDW tools and the Avatar preview.

sections.title: Safe editing
steps: Load the exact character through Sync.
Make bounded Character, Item, Spell, Recipe, or Quest changes.
Click See changes when you want the 3D preview to refresh.
Save through Sync so checksum, backup, write, and reparse verification run.

sections.title: Character Editor
sections.body: Appearance controls and wrapping color swatches live on the left, the stable 3D preview stays centered, and compatible equipped items remain on the right.

sections.title: Preview behavior
sections.body: Draft edits do not reset the 3D model automatically. See changes is the explicit preview boundary; camera and pose controls remain preview-only.

sections.title: Item Editor
sections.body: Canonical and modded definitions share one identity repository. Right-click menus are constrained to the visible application window.

sections.title: Discovery and associations
sections.body: Discovery identifies supported saves and enough metadata to distinguish characters. When names repeat, compare source paths and timestamps before associating a save with a profile.

sections.title: Verified write sequence
steps: Parse the selected save.
Create and validate a bounded draft.
Write a recovery backup.
Replace the target atomically where supported.
Reparse the saved result and report verification.

sections.title: Recovery
sections.body: If a write fails verification, preserve the visible error and use the generated backup rather than repeatedly saving over the same target.

tips: Undo, Redo, and Revert affect the draft.
Save Character creates a recovery backup.
Export uses the portable character package flow.

pages.title: Server & WebHost
pages.summary: Dedicated profiles, runtime startup, heartbeats, and remote WebGUI.
pages.intro: Hosted Worlds own presentation, save/config snapshots, mod state, and Sync settings while sharing the machine-level dedicated runtime.

sections.title: Fluid startup sequence
steps: Resolve the selected profile and desired revision.
Materialize save, configuration, and managed mods.
Launch and verify the dedicated process.
Start and verify the World-owned Sync listener.
Publish only after runtime and Sync evidence pass.

sections.title: WebHost
sections.body: WebHost projects the public browser, receives authenticated heartbeats, exposes public-safe APIs, and can pair remote administration when enabled.

sections.title: Public safety
sections.body: Public surfaces may show identity, artwork, badges, counts, routes, and capability. Credentials and private configuration are never directory fields.

sections.title: Remote administration
sections.body: Remote control is separate from discovery and requires an authenticated session plus explicit World-scoped permissions.

sections.title: Runtime ownership
sections.body: The application supervises processes it launches and retains enough state to reattach safely. A returned button or toast does not prove the server reached healthy running state.

sections.title: Stopping and cleanup
sections.body: Stop targets the owned process tree and verifies cleanup. If verification fails, the unresolved state remains visible instead of being reported as a success.

sections.title: Updates and rollback
sections.body: Runtime updates identify the desired revision, verify installed state, and protect recoverable save and configuration data before binaries change.

tips: Stop verifies process-tree cleanup.
Heartbeat declarations have a TTL.
Website and Remote Access remain independent switches.

pages.title: Mods, Items & Spawner
pages.summary: Master repository, profile copies, custom items, and spawning.
pages.image_alt: Master mod repository and profile actions
pages.intro: Mod placement and item metadata remain profile-aware without turning custom content into global vanilla data.

sections.title: Master repository
steps: Edit Master changes only the canonical repository payload.
Edit Profile changes one deployed copy.
Publish as Master updates the canonical payload without overwriting profiles.
Pull Master replaces only the profile you choose.

sections.title: Managed editor
sections.body: Supported text files use atomic bounded writes. Binary and oversized files stay visible but read-only.

sections.title: Modded items
sections.body: PersistenceID, ITEM_NAME, display name, category, equipment slot, stack metadata, description, and icon aliases merge into the shared Item Editor and Spawner repository.

sections.title: Recommended mods
sections.body: Each recommendation uses one banner placard, the mod name, and its Nexus Mods or Steam source identity.

sections.title: Spawner
sections.body: The server Spawner consumes the same normalized item record and requires an explicit item, count, and target before issuing a bounded command.

sections.title: Inventory safety
sections.body: Equipment, action bar, storage, and inventory slots validate category, stack, and equipment compatibility. Right-click menus remain inside the visible application window and reposition near edges.

sections.title: Repository refresh
sections.body: After supported mod manifests are added or changed, refresh the canonical item repository so Item Editor and Spawner consume the same normalized definitions and source provenance.

sections.title: Command boundary
sections.body: Spawner commands require an exact item, bounded amount, and explicit runtime target. Review the summary before issuing a command.

tips: Profile tags and load order remain profile-specific.
Pull Master is deliberately destructive only to the chosen copy.
Spawner definitions can come from portable mod manifests.

pages.title: Profiles & Associations
pages.summary: Keep Worlds, characters, mods, saves, and launch policy in intentional groups.
pages.intro: Profiles prevent unrelated play setups from silently sharing mutable files. A profile records what belongs together and gives every Appy the same bounded working context.

sections.title: What a profile owns
sections.body: A profile may reference a World, character saves, a profile-specific mod deployment, launch settings, artwork, connection details, and hosting metadata. Machine-level runtimes remain shared where duplication would be unsafe.

sections.title: Creating a profile
steps: Choose the intended play mode.
Select or import the World save.
Associate the correct characters.
Choose an empty, detected, or master-derived mod deployment.
Review the summary before saving.

sections.title: Switching profiles
sections.body: Switching changes the active context but does not overwrite another profile. File materialization, Pull Master, and migrations remain explicit actions.

sections.title: Portable data
sections.body: Supported exports carry bounded metadata and selected content. Credentials, tokens, and machine-specific secrets are not portable profile fields.

sections.title: Removal and recovery
sections.body: Deleting application metadata, moving a profile to trash, and deleting an underlying save are different operations. Read the confirmation scope and preserve important saves.

screenshots.description: Show identity, play mode, World, character, and mod association fields.

screenshots.title: Profile switcher and active context
screenshots.description: Show how the active profile is identified before a destructive operation.

tips: Separate incompatible mod sets into profiles.
Profile removal and save deletion are different.
Export before large migrations.

pages.title: Networking & Remote Access
pages.summary: Separate game, Sync, directory, website, and authenticated remote-control routes.
pages.intro: Dragonwilds Sync uses distinct network responsibilities. Keeping them separate makes exposure, permissions, and troubleshooting understandable.

sections.title: Route responsibilities
sections.body: Game traffic serves players. Sync negotiates identity and managed content. Heartbeats publish public-safe state. Website hosting serves browser pages. Remote administration performs authenticated control.

sections.title: Bindings and ports
sections.body: A configured or listening port does not prove public reachability. Local firewall policy, router behavior, tunnels, and provider routing all contribute.

sections.title: Website versus Remote Access
sections.body: Website publication and Remote Access are independent switches. Publishing a World page must never silently enable administrative control.

sections.title: Authentication and secrets
sections.body: Remote administration requires an authenticated session and explicit World-scoped permissions. Secrets do not belong in public manifests, directory rows, logs, or screenshots.

sections.title: Troubleshooting order
steps: Confirm the intended service runs locally.
Verify its bound address and port.
Check local firewall and security software.
Verify router, tunnel, or provider routing.
Confirm the client uses the expected endpoint and identity.

screenshots.title: Network responsibility map
screenshots.description: Diagram game, Sync, heartbeat, website, and remote-administration routes.

screenshots.title: Remote Access configuration
screenshots.description: Show independent website and remote-control switches plus authentication state.

tips: A listening port is not automatically public.
Website access does not imply administrative access.
Never include secrets in screenshots.

pages.title: Settings, Themes & Integrations
pages.summary: Control appearance, paths, policy, integrations, and durable preferences.
pages.intro: Settings owns durable application preferences and identifies whether a change applies immediately, on next navigation, or after restart.

sections.title: Dark, White, and Glass
sections.body: Dark and White choose the color foundation. Glass is an independent treatment that adds blurred surfaces, stained-glass color, depth, and atmospheric backgrounds while preserving the chosen foundation.

sections.title: Paths and discovery
sections.body: Installation, save, runtime, and repository paths are validated before storage. Changing a path does not move data unless an explicit migration is offered.

sections.title: Integrations
sections.body: Nexus Mods, Steam, Discord, tunnels, and related services expose separate capabilities and authentication requirements. A saved account label is not proof of a healthy connection.

sections.title: Safety policy
sections.body: Automatic updates, backups, publication defaults, experimental features, and remote permissions use explicit controls with visible consequences.

sections.title: Reset and recovery
sections.body: Reset distinguishes appearance preferences from paths, profiles, credentials, and application-owned data. Export important configuration before a broad reset.

screenshots.title: Dark, White, and Glass controls
screenshots.description: Show color mode and the independent Glass treatment with representative previews.

screenshots.title: Integration status
screenshots.description: Show service capabilities, connected state, and safe credential actions.

tips: Glass is a treatment, not a replacement theme.
A path change does not automatically migrate files.
Export configuration before reset.

pages.title: Updates, Diagnostics & Recovery
pages.summary: Understand versions, health checks, logs, backups, trash, and recovery boundaries.
pages.intro: Maintenance tools explain what is installed, what the application owns, and how to recover when a staged operation cannot complete.

sections.title: Application updates
sections.body: Update checks compare channel and installed version against an authoritative release source. Download, verification, installation, and restart are separate stages.

sections.title: Runtime health
sections.body: Game, dedicated server, UE4SS, RuneSchema, and helper runtimes can have different authorities. Health reports identify component, desired state, detected state, and recommended action.

sections.title: Logs and diagnostics
sections.body: Use the narrowest relevant log first: operation, Sync, server runtime, integration, or application console. Remove credentials and private addresses before sharing.

sections.title: Backups and trash
sections.body: Editor backups protect write targets and application trash protects supported records. Neither replaces an external backup of irreplaceable Worlds and characters.

sections.title: Recovery order
steps: Stop repeating the failed operation.
Record the error and active profile.
Confirm a backup or trash entry exists.
Restore the smallest affected component.
Run discovery or validation before relaunching.

screenshots.title: Backups, trash, and recovery
screenshots.description: Show recovery points and a scoped restore confirmation.

tips: Do not share secrets in diagnostics.
Restore the smallest scope first.

pages.title: Website, World Builder & Preview
pages.summary: Browse Worlds, draft profiles, preview the launcher, download releases, and maintain Helpy.
pages.intro: The GitHub Pages site is the public companion to the desktop application. It hosts releases, community destinations, the public World directory, World Builder, Preview Launcher, and the shared Helpy guide.

sections.title: Shared Helpy
sections.body: The website and desktop application render help/manifest.json from the webpage branch. Editing one JSON source updates both after Pages deployment.

sections.title: World Builder
sections.body: The browser builder creates a local World Draft with presentation, rules, mod families, and supported attachments. Desktop performs final validation and adoption.

sections.title: Preview Launcher
sections.body: The read-only launcher preview renders representative Appys from assets/launcher-preview.json. It demonstrates navigation and states without local filesystem, account, save, or runtime access.

sections.title: Public Servers and downloads
sections.body: The directory uses bounded live data and a baked fallback snapshot. Release downloads resolve from GitHub release metadata and identify their artifact and channel.

sections.title: Adding a screenshot
steps: Place the file under renderer/assets/help on webpage.
Find its screenshot slot in help/manifest.json.
Add an image property such as ../assets/help/41-player-setup.png.
Optionally add concise alt text.
Push webpage and let the Pages workflow validate and publish.

screenshots.description: Show navigation, releases, World tools, WebGUI, and community destinations.

screenshots.title: JSON Preview Launcher
screenshots.description: Show the Appy rail, active workspace, representative cards, and read-only notice.

tips: Helpy content is edited once in JSON.
World Builder exports a draft, not a running server.
Preview Launcher never performs real operations.

pages.title: Linux Platforms & Detection
pages.summary: Rich distro identity, native hosting, Proton/Wine clients, and privacy-safe directory badges.
pages.image_alt: Placeholder for the Linux distribution detection workspace in Settings
pages.intro: Dragonwilds Sync reads standard os-release metadata to identify Linux hosts without publishing machine-specific or user-specific details.

sections.title: Detection sources
steps: Read /etc/os-release first and /usr/lib/os-release as the fallback.
Normalize ID and ID_LIKE aliases into a canonical distro and broader family.
Keep friendly name, version, codename, exact/fallback icon, and Ubuntu-baseline support status.
Fall back to a known ancestor mark or the generic Linux mark when a derivative has no dedicated artwork.

sections.title: Recognized distribution families
sections.body: The baked catalog covers Ubuntu and Debian derivatives, Fedora/RHEL families, openSUSE/SUSE, Arch and gaming derivatives, plus Gentoo, Void, Alpine, NixOS, Guix, Clear Linux, Solus, Mageia, OpenMandriva, and Slackware.

sections.title: Native server mode
sections.body: A native Linux dedicated server uses RSDragonwildsServer.sh and LinuxServer configuration. Native ELF trees do not receive Win64 UE4SS or RuneSchema DLLs.

sections.title: Proton and Wine mode
sections.body: The retail game client remains Windows PE x64 under Proton/Wine. That ABI can use the signed Win64 UE4SS and RuneSchema runtime variants with an explicit executable, compatibility prefix, and DLL override policy.

sections.title: World directory privacy
sections.body: Heartbeats may publish OS family, friendly distro name, version, family, icon key, and support flags. Kernel strings, machine names, usernames, executable paths, and local directories are intentionally excluded.

sections.title: Unknown derivatives
sections.body: An unknown ID is not treated as failure. ID_LIKE ancestry provides family and artwork fallback while distro_known remains false so the UI can honestly show that the match is inherited.

tips: Ubuntu is the supported native-server baseline; other distributions remain visible as community paths.
Host distro and game ABI are separate decisions.
Use the Settings preview to compare exact, derivative, and family-fallback detections.

pages.title: For Modders
pages.summary: A line-by-line ID.txt contract and safe ZIP-to-RSDWL packaging guide.
pages.intro: Mod authors can give Sync stable identity, runtime, link, tag, custom-item, and icon metadata without executable package instructions.

sections.title: Canonical ID.txt
sections.body: Place UTF-8 ID.txt at the effective mod root. HOTLOAD = YES is valid as the only line and normalizes to hotload_capable true with runtime_role both and empty optional fields. The parser is case-insensitive, bounded to 512 KiB, accepts colon or equals delimiters, and retains read compatibility for identity.txt and identities.txt.

sections.title: Drop-in ID.txt discovery
sections.body: A normal mod folder, ZIP, or manually packed .rsdwl may carry ID.txt at its effective payload root. Sync reads it during staged installation and every inventory scan, including through optional wrapper folders. If HOTLOAD = YES is the only line, hotload_capable becomes true, runtime_role defaults to both, and omitted metadata remains empty or uses inventory/folder presentation fallbacks.

sections.title: Identity fields
sections.body: ModId, Name, Version, Revision, Author, RuntimeRole, HotloadCapable, Description, Tags, web links, and repeatable Item records are normalized into safe launcher metadata.

sections.title: Item identity
sections.body: Each Item record may declare ITEM Name, PersistenceID, DisplayName, Icon, AssetPath, and ModId. PersistenceID is the cross-source merge key used by Item Editor and Spawner.

sections.title: Icon-bearing mod folders
sections.body: Use items/manifest.json, items/icon-manifest.json, and relative items/icons assets. Sync records each generated icon path, SHA-256, and media type and rejects paths escaping the import root.

sections.title: Manual and canonical RSDWL
sections.body: A valid mod ZIP may be manually renamed to .rsdwl when it contains a recognizable UE4SS, RuneSchema, or PAK layout and no root manifest.json. Sync labels it compatibility-mod-archive and validated false. Canonical application packages that include a root manifest remain on the strict payload-index, checksum, provenance, and signature validation path.

sections.title: Full field guide
sections.body: Open the For Modders tab in the website navigation for copy-ready examples, every accepted field and alias, parser order, folder diagrams, and icon checklist.

tips: HOTLOAD = YES works by itself; metadata is declarative and never executed.
Do not place passwords, tokens, credentials, or local machine paths in ID.txt.
Manual .rsdwl mod archives remain unvalidated compatibility packages; canonical exports retain signed package validation.
